name: Wireless & Bluetooth Security
tagline: WiFi capture and cracking, PMKID and precomputed tables, RF spectrum analysis, WPS auditing, and Bluetooth — all framed for labs and gear you own or are authorized to audit.

tools.name: airmon-ng
tools.desc: Script from the aircrack-ng suite that flips a supported chipset into monitor mode (and back), kills interfering processes, and reports adapter capabilities.
tools.when: First step of any authorized Wi-Fi test: enable monitor mode on the adapter you own and confirm chipset/driver support before capture or injection.

tools.name: iw
tools.desc: The nl80211 wireless CLI: lists radios and phy capabilities and sets interface modes (monitor/managed) without legacy wrapper scripts.
tools.when: When airmon-ng's heuristics stall, set mode=monitor by hand on an interface you control and verify the phy supports injection.

tools.name: macchanger
tools.desc: Spoofs a wireless interface's MAC address so lab captures originate from an anonymized, disposable local address.
tools.when: Before a capture or wifite run in your lab when you want a clean identity that is trivially reset between tests.

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.desc: Classic packet capture tool; on a monitor interface it proves the card actually sees 802.11 beacons, probe requests, and management frames.
tools.when: Smoke-test the adapter: run tcpdump on mon0 and confirm frames before starting a long airodump or Kismet session on your own hardware.

tools.name: airguard
tools.desc: Wireless defense & monitoring suite — WIDS sensor, deauth/evil-twin/rogue-AP detection, beacon anomaly scan, WPA3 survey.
tools.when: Detecting rogue APs and deauth floods in your own wireless perimeter.

tools.name: airodump-ng
tools.desc: Channel-by-channel capture of BSSIDs, clients, signal, and encryption; logs raw PCAPc and collects probe requests and association traffic from nearby APs you can hear.
tools.when: Start discovery here on hardware you control: target channels, capture beacon/probe data, and note handshake material for later offline work.

tools.name: horst
tools.desc: Lightweight ncurses 802.11 monitor with channel scanning, signal histograms, and per-client statistics, no daemon or web UI required.
tools.when: A minimal TUI for quick signal and channel-noise checks mid-test in your lab when Kismet is overkill.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/br101/horst && cd horst && make && sudo make install

tools.name: wiair
tools.desc: Byte-exact 802.11/BLE frame crafting & parsing framework; offline-only and safety-gated.
tools.when: Building raw wireless frames for protocol research and WIDS/emitter lab work.

tools.name: Kismet
tools.desc: Multi-protocol passive detector with server + web UI; tracks 802.11, Bluetooth, and SDR sources and logs probe traffic for long-running surveys.
tools.when: Long-running passive mapping of your authorized airspace, or intrusion-detection-style monitoring over your own test environment.

tools.name: Wireshark
tools.desc: Universal dissector with deep 802.11 and EAPOL support; supply the PMK to decrypt WPA traffic you captured from your own APs.
tools.when: Post-capture dissection of handshakes, probe requests, and Bluetooth frames from gear you own.

tools.name: wifite2
tools.desc: Automated lab auditor: scans, lets you pick a target you own, then drives deauth, handshake capture, and cracking (or WPS work via reaver/bully) from one menu.
tools.when: Repeatable capture-to-crack runs against your own APs where one command replaces a long manual chain.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/derv82/wifite2.git && cd wifite2 && sudo python3 setup.py install

tools.name: aireplay-ng
tools.desc: Frame injection and replay from aircrack-ng: sends deauthentication frames and replays captured packets to force a fresh 4-way handshake from an idle station.
tools.when: In your lab, deauth a stationary test client to accelerate handshake capture and PSK policy validation on APs you manage.

tools.name: mdk4
tools.desc: Multi-purpose 802.11 tool with aggressive deauthentication, probe-testing, and fuzzing modes (mdk4 w / m / f) for validating client and AP reactions.
tools.when: Stress the deauth resistance of APs you own and verify clients reconnect cleanly and re-associate after interference.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/aircrack-ng/mdk4 && cd mdk4 && make && sudo make install

tools.name: hcxdumptool
tools.desc: Raw PCAPNG capture of PMKID and EAPOL material using a single adapter; PMKID needs no connected client and no deauthentication.
tools.when: On APs you own that expose PMKID, grab the token passively and skip the whole deauth-and-reassociate dance.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/ZerBea/hcxdumptool.git && cd hcxdumptool && make && sudo make install

tools.name: hcxtools
tools.desc: Converts hcxdumptool PCAPNG captures into hashcat/john-ready hash formats (mode 22000), filtering duplicates and invalid entries.
tools.when: After capture, normalize EAPOL/PMKID material into 22000 format so GPU testing can start on your own hashes.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/ZerBea/hcxtools.git && cd hcxtools && make && sudo make install

tools.name: aircrack-ng
tools.desc: The suite's cracking core validates WPA/WPA2 handshakes against wordlists (and PTW for WEP), verifying recovered keys against the captured material.
tools.when: Offline verification of PSK strength from captures taken against your own access points.

tools.name: hashcat
tools.desc: GPU password cracker with native WPA-PBKDF2-PMKID+EAPOL kernels (mode 22000) for turning captured handshake hashes into keys at high speed.
tools.when: When masks/rules outgrow aircrack-ng and you have a GPU available for faster PMK derivation in your lab.

tools.name: cowpatty
tools.desc: Wordlist PSK verifier that confirms candidate passphrases against captured handshake material without extra dependencies.
tools.when: Clean no-frills confirmation that a candidate passphrase matches your capture before moving on.

tools.name: airolib-ng
tools.desc: Builds precomputed PMK tables keyed by (ESSID, password) from wordlists and serves hashes to aircrack-ng for instant reuse.
tools.when: Repeatedly audit the same ESSID: precompute its PMK table once, then crack many captured handshakes instantly in your lab.

tools.name: genpmk
tools.desc: cowpatty's companion that precomputes the per-ESSID PMK seed file from a wordlist for fast later handshake verification.
tools.when: One-off ESSID precompute when you do not want the full airolib database machinery.

tools.name: wash
tools.desc: Passive scanner for WPS-enabled access points: reports WPS state and lockout status without launching an active registrar exchange.
tools.when: Recon your own estate for WPS-enabled APs before deciding a PIN audit is even worthwhile.

tools.name: Reaver
tools.desc: The reference WPS registrar brute-forcer: probes PIN transaction logic and, on vulnerable lab routers, recovers the WPS PIN and derived WPA-PSK.
tools.when: Confirm your lab AP's WPS lockout and PIN policy — most modern routers lock out after failures, which is the outcome you want to verify.

tools.name: Bully
tools.desc: C reimplementation of the WPS PIN attack with more forgiving association handling and clearer logging than reaver.
tools.when: When reaver stalls against your own AP, bully's retry logic often completes the audit where reaver cannot.

tools.name: pixiewps
tools.desc: Offline WPS computation tool (R1/R2/RB) that takes the e-S1/e-S2 nonces captured by reaver/bully and recovers the PIN without brute force.
tools.when: On older WPS APs you own with predictable RNG, run pixiewps over a reaver capture to recover the PIN in seconds instead of hours.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/wiire/pixiewps && cd pixiewps && make && sudo make install

tools.name: airbase-ng
tools.desc: Creates 802.11 software access points from a monitor-mode card; the primitive behind most fake-AP tests, including WEP/WPA emulation and injection.
tools.when: Stand up a disposable simulated AP in your own lab for behavior tests and client-device compatibility checks.

tools.name: hostapd-wpe
tools.desc: Patched hostapd that adds WPA enterprise (PEAP/MSCHAPv2) credential capture for controlled authentication tests in your lab.
tools.when: Building an enterprise authentication test rig against client configs you control, capturing challenge/response pairs for offline review.
tools.install: git clone https://gitlab.com/kalilinux/packages/hostapd-wpe && cd hostapd-wpe && sudo make -C hostapd install

tools.name: wifiphisher
tools.desc: Carries out evil-twin attacks with a real captive portal: clones a target AP you own, then serves phishing templates to harvest credentials and PMKID.
tools.when: Demo rogue-AP and social-engineering tradecraft only against APs and clients you own or explicitly control in the lab.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/wifiphisher/wifiphisher && cd wifiphisher && sudo python3 setup.py install

tools.name: fluxion
tools.desc: Evil-twin toolkit that deauths a target you own, runs a cloned fake AP, and feeds a captive-login page to collect passphrases.
tools.when: Scripted WPA2 capture plus captive-portal phishing against your own APs and test accounts.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/FluxionNetwork/fluxion && cd fluxion && sudo ./fluxion.sh

tools.name: eaphammer
tools.desc: Targeted evil-twin and enterprise attack tool with WPA/WPA2 enterprise automation, KARMA, and credential-database harvesting for lab demos.
tools.when: Enterprise (802.1X) test scenarios against your own lab RADIUS and client fleets before touching production gear.

tools.name: bettercap
tools.desc: Host-side network and monitoring framework whose BLE module runs recon, sniffs, and offers a ble.proxy that can pose as a peripheral for lab devices.
tools.when: Scriptable, host-based BLE enumeration and proxy testing of your own peripherals without dedicated sniffing hardware.

tools.name: Ubertooth
tools.desc: Open 2.4 GHz radio plus host software for Bluetooth capture and injection; follows Classic BT hopping patterns and BLE channels on the Ubertooth One dongle.
tools.when: Hardware-level analysis of hop patterns, advertising data, and pairing behavior of peripherals you own.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/greatscottgadgets/ubertooth && cd ubertooth/host && mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. && make && sudo make install

tools.name: btlejack
tools.desc: Sniffs and interacts with BLE connections via nRF24-family USB dongles; supports jamming and session recovery from previously captured keys.
tools.when: Low-cost BLE session auditing of your own accessories — map advertising channels and check for key reuse across connections.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/virtualabs/btlejack && cd btlejack && make && sudo make install

tools.name: BlueZ
tools.desc: Linux's Bluetooth stack: bluetoothctl, btmon, hcitool, and gatttool expose controller state, HCI packets, and GATT services.
tools.when: Free host-side visibility before reaching for RF hardware; btmon gives clean pairing and connection traces for your own adapters.

tools.name: bt_audit (BTSD)
tools.desc: The BTSD Bluetooth audit suite: psm_scan maps L2CAP PSM services and rfcomm_scan enumerates RFCOMM channels on local or paired devices.
tools.when: A quick authorized inventory of services your own BT peripherals expose before deeper hardware testing.
tools.install: Download bt_audit-0.1.1.tar.gz from betaversion.net, extract, and run make in the src directory

tools.name: Proxmark3 (Iceman)
tools.desc: Proxmark3 hardware plus the Iceman project firmware: read, clone, and analyze low- and high-frequency tags including MIFARE, ISO14443, and iCLASS.
tools.when: Physical badge and tag auditing of assets you own — sniff reader/tag sessions and validate card copy resistance.

tools.name: libnfc
tools.desc: Portable NFC library with CLI tools (nfc-list, nfc-read, nfc-mfclassic) for enumerating and reading tags through USB readers.
tools.when: With an ACR122U-class reader, enumerate and read blocks on cards you own without dedicated hardware.

tools.name: mfoc
tools.desc: The classic MIFARE Classic hardnested tool: exploits leaked (weak) keys to recover the full key set of a card you own.
tools.when: Recover all sectors of a weak-key MIFARE Classic card in your lab for badge cloning and access-control red-team tests.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/nfc-tools/mfoc && cd mfoc && ./autogen.sh && ./configure && make && sudo make install

tools.name: mfcuk
tools.desc: MIFARE Classic dark-side attack tool that recovers keys on cards whose PRNG hands out predictable nonces.
tools.when: When mfoc's hardnested path fails against a card you own, mfcuk's dark-side vector is the fallback.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/nfc-tools/mfcuk && cd mfcuk && ./autogen.sh && ./configure && make && sudo make install

tools.name: RTL-SDR
tools.desc: Cheap USB software-defined radio receiver: drivers plus rtl_test, rtl_fm, and rtl_tcp for raw IQ sampling and streaming.
tools.when: The base RF capture hardware and tooling: stream IQ captures into gqrx or inspectrum for analysis of signals in your own environment.

tools.name: gqrx
tools.desc: GNU Radio-based desktop receiver that demodulates and displays spectrum and waterfall from an SDR dongle.
tools.when: Interactively scan ISM bands and identify transmitters or interference sources before blaming your own Wi-Fi gear.

tools.name: inspectrum
tools.desc: Offline analysis of recorded IQ or audio: renders interactive water-falls to identify modulation, timing, and packet structure.
tools.when: After recording bursts with rtl_sdr, step through symbols to identify the modulation type before deeper decoding.

tools.name: GNU Radio
tools.desc: Flow-graph framework for designing and running custom demodulators and decoders; the engine underneath gqrx and many SDR toolchains.
tools.when: When you must decode a custom protocol from captured samples of signals you are authorized to receive.
